info.name: ATW Backend — Worker
info.description:
# ATW Backend — Worker

Admin-facing worker lifecycle management: core profile CRUD, designation/skill assignment (a worker holds up to 3 designations, exactly one primary, and only skills that belong to one of those designations), the `REGISTERED` → `KYC_PENDING` → `ACTIVE` → `SUSPENDED`/`INACTIVE`/`BLACKLISTED` status lifecycle (with its own explicit-target-status, reason-required, super-admin-gated rules), bulk status/delete, CSV export, and three address/bank-detail/notes sub-resources. This is the richest controller in the codebase - every rule below is pulled directly from `WorkerService`'s own Javadoc, not guessed.

Worker KYC (Aadhaar/PAN submission and document review) and face-biometric enrollment are two *separate* modules/controllers (`kyc`, `faceauth`) - this controller only ever reads their already-computed, read-only summaries (`kycStatus`, `faceEnrollment`) and, in one place (Worker KYC Bridge), *consumes* an already-`VERIFIED` Aadhaar e-KYC verification to upgrade an existing worker. See **ATW-Worker-KYC.postman_collection.json** / **ATW-Worker-FaceAuth.postman_collection.json** for those modules' own endpoints.

**Run order:** Get a bearer token first (Login / Verify OTP in ATW-Auth-Account), then seed the reference data Create Worker needs from ATW-Masterdata: a Department (required) and at least one Designation (required - needs an Industry first); Industry and Skill beyond that are optional. Worker Profile's **Create Worker** then populates `{{workerId}}`, which every other folder in this collection depends on. Save **Worker Deletion** for last.

**Shared conventions across every request in this collection:**
- Every endpoint requires `Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}` **and** its own specific `workers.*` permission (`workers.view_comments` for the two Notes requests) - there is no endpoint here usable by a bare authenticated caller the way Masterdata's two Geography lookups are.
- `{id}` in every path below is a worker id (UUID); an unknown one always comes back `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, message "Worker not found" - documented once here, not repeated on every request.
- Two response shapes exist for a worker: the full `WorkerResponse` (Get Worker, and every write endpoint that returns a worker - short-lived signed profile-photo URL, full `faceEnrollment` object, `kycStatus`) and the lighter `WorkerSummaryResponse` (the List/Export row - no signed URL, no `faceEnrollment` object, just `hasProfilePhoto`/`faceEnrolledAt`). `kycStatus` and face-enrollment data are both **read-only** summaries resolved from the separate `kyc`/`faceauth` modules - never editable through this controller.
- Address, Bank Detail, and Designations/Skills updates are all **full replaces**: a field you omit is cleared to `null` (Address/Bank Detail) or the whole set is replaced (Designations/Skills) - never a partial patch of just the fields you send. Core profile Update is different - most of its fields are required on every call.
- Status changes always take an **explicit target status** (`workers.toggle_status`), never a blind toggle - the same reasoning as Masterdata's own status endpoints. `REGISTERED`/`KYC_PENDING` can never be set through this API (reached only automatically, via KYC verification); a `reason` is required for `SUSPENDED`/`BLACKLISTED`/`INACTIVE`; entering **or** leaving `BLACKLISTED` additionally requires the caller to be a super-admin.
- Deletion is a **soft** delete (`deletedAt`) - never a real SQL `DELETE` - and is refused while the worker is `ACTIVE`. Every satellite row (address, bank detail, notes, status history, KYC, face enrollment) is left untouched, and the worker's mobile number becomes available for reuse.
- `POST .../bulk-status` and `POST .../bulk-delete` both take a batch of ids and process each independently - partial success is normal; check `data.failures[]` for which id was skipped and why - same convention as every bulk endpoint in ATW-Masterdata.
- Profile-photo upload/removal uses the exact same multipart validation Masterdata's icon uploads use (field name `file`; `image/png`/`image/jpeg`/`image/webp` only, cross-checked against the file's actual leading bytes; 2MB cap; replacing deletes the old blob; short-lived ~15 minute signed URL) - see ATW-Masterdata's Industries folder description for the full security rationale, not repeated here.
- `GET /{id}/address/{type}` and `GET /{id}/bank-detail` return an all-`null`/`false` row rather than `404` when nothing has been saved yet for that worker - the sub-resource simply doesn't exist yet; that's not an error.
- `accountNumber` on bank detail is masked (e.g. `**********5678`) unless the caller also holds `kyc.view_sensitive` - the same sensitivity gate the `kyc` module uses for Aadhaar/PAN numbers.
- Saved **error**-response examples below illustrate that error's JSON *shape*; a few (a 409 duplicate, a bulk endpoint's partial-failure example) assume different seed data than whatever the example request body shows, same as ATW-Masterdata's own duplicate-name examples - they are not meant to be reproduced byte-for-byte by replaying that exact request.

Every endpoint is versioned under `/api/v1/` and returns the same envelope:

```
{ "success": boolean, "data": <payload> | null, "error": <ApiError> | null }
```

`ApiError` shape: `{"code": string, "message": string, "fieldErrors": [{"field","message"}] | null, "timestamp": ISO-8601 string, "traceId": string | null}`. `fieldErrors` is populated only for `VALIDATION_ERROR` responses that came from `@Valid` request-body validation; it's `null`/omitted for every other error, including other `VALIDATION_ERROR` responses raised programmatically (e.g. "Unknown permission code(s)"). `traceId` echoes the `X-Correlation-Id` request header when present — include it when reporting a bug.

## Running this collection

Select the **ATW Backend - Local** environment first.

1. Run **Login** / **Verify OTP** from **ATW-Auth-Account.postman_collection.json** to populate `{{accessToken}}` - every request below requires it, plus its own `workers.*` permission.
2. From **ATW-Masterdata.postman_collection.json**, run **Create Department** (→ `{{departmentId}}`) and **Create Industry** (→ `{{industryId}}`, optional) → **Create Designation** (→ `{{designationId}}`, needs an industry) → **Create Skill** (→ `{{skillId}}`, optional, needs a designation). Worker Profile's Create Worker needs a real `departmentId` and at least one real `designationId`; `industryId`/`skillId` are optional.
3. **Worker Profile → Create Worker** populates `{{workerId}}` - every folder below needs it.
4. **Worker Status**, **Worker Designations & Skills**, **Worker Photo**, **Worker Address**, **Worker Bank Detail**, and **Worker Notes** can then run in any order against the same `{{workerId}}`.
5. **Worker KYC Bridge → Complete Aadhaar Verification** additionally needs a real `{{verificationId}}` for an already-`VERIFIED`, not-yet-consumed Aadhaar check - see **ATW-Worker-KYC.postman_collection.json** (a sibling collection) for how one is produced. This request is independent of everything else here - skip it if you don't have one yet.
6. Run **Worker Deletion** (**Delete Worker** / **Bulk Delete Workers**) **last** - several folders above need `{{workerId}}` to still exist, and Delete additionally needs the worker's status to already be something other than `ACTIVE` (Worker Status's own **Change Worker Status** request, earlier in this run, already takes care of that).

## Error codes that can appear on (almost) any endpoint

These are produced centrally — by `GlobalExceptionHandler`, by Spring Security's entry point / access-denied handler, or by the two security filters that run before a controller is even reached — so they are **not** re-documented on every individual request below; only an endpoint's *specific* codes and triggers are. Two pairs are easy to confuse and worth reading carefully:

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 | A `@Valid` request-body field failed Bean Validation (`fieldErrors[]` present), or a service-level input check failed (no `fieldErrors`). |
| `MALFORMED_REQUEST` | 400 | Request body is missing or isn't valid JSON. |
| `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE` | 415 | `Content-Type` isn't `application/json`. |
| `UNAUTHENTICATED` | 401 | **No bearer token was presented at all**, or it's malformed/expired/signature-invalid. Produced by Spring Security itself, before any controller runs. |
| `UNAUTHORIZED` | 401 | A **business-level** auth failure on an endpoint that doesn't require a token in the first place — bad login credentials, a locked/disabled account, an invalid refresh/reset/invite token. Same HTTP status as `UNAUTHENTICATED` above, different meaning: this means "the token/credential you supplied is bad", not "you supplied nothing". |
| `SESSION_REVOKED` | 401 | The bearer token parses fine, but the admin's `security_version` has moved on since it was issued (password changed/reset, or their role assignment changed), or the account is no longer `ACTIVE`. The client must discard tokens and log in again — refreshing won't help, the refresh token was revoked too. |
| `MUST_CHANGE_PASSWORD` | 403 | Authenticated, but the token's `mustChangePassword` flag is set and this isn't `/admin/account/me` or `/admin/account/change-password`. |
| `ACCESS_DENIED` | 403 | Authenticated, but lacking the specific permission the endpoint requires. |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | Too many requests to one of the 6 public, abuse-prone auth endpoints from the same IP within the window — default 10 requests/60s, **per endpoint**, not pooled across them. |
| `NOT_FOUND` | 404 | The **URL itself** doesn't match any endpoint (a routing miss — typo'd path, wrong version prefix, etc). |
| `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | The URL is valid, but the specific id in it (a staff id, role id, ...) doesn't exist. Different from `NOT_FOUND` above — don't conflate "no such route" with "no such record". |
| `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` | 405 | Right URL, wrong HTTP verb. |
| `BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION` | 422 | Input is syntactically well-formed but violates a business rule (e.g. "system roles cannot be modified", a privilege-escalation attempt, self/super-admin protection). |
| `CONFLICT` | 409 | Either an endpoint's own duplicate check (most common — a friendlier, specific message), or a generic last-resort safety net when a unique-constraint violation reaches the database despite an earlier application-level check passing (a genuine race between two concurrent requests) — that fallback case always carries the same generic message, regardless of which field collided. |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | 500 | Unexpected failure. Full detail (stack trace) is logged server-side against the same `traceId` returned to the client; never returned in the response body itself. |

## Documentation cross-references

- **ATW-Auth-Account.postman_collection.json** — login/2FA; needed for `{{accessToken}}` before anything here will work.
- **ATW-RBAC-Staff.postman_collection.json** — role/permission management; grant a role the `workers.*` permissions this collection exercises.
- **ATW-Masterdata.postman_collection.json** — departments/industries/designations/skills/geography; Create Worker, Assign Designations/Skills, and Update Address all reference ids created there (`{{departmentId}}`, `{{industryId}}`, `{{designationId}}`, `{{skillId}}`, `{{stateId}}`, `{{cityId}}`).
- **ATW-Worker-KYC.postman_collection.json** / **ATW-Worker-FaceAuth.postman_collection.json** — the Aadhaar/PAN KYC submission-and-review flow and face-biometric enrollment live in their own controllers/modules; this controller only ever reads their already-computed `kycStatus`/`faceEnrollment` summaries, and in one place (Worker KYC Bridge) consumes an already-verified Aadhaar check.
- `FRONTEND_HANDOVER.md` — frontend integration conventions (signed-URL/file-upload pattern, envelope shape) that apply here too.
- `HANDOVER.md` — Azure deployment context.

item.name: Worker Profile
item.description: Core worker CRUD under `/api/v1/admin/workers` - list/search, single-worker detail, create, replace-profile update, and CSV export. Permission is per request: `workers.view` (List, Get), `workers.create` (Create), `workers.edit` (Update), `workers.export` (Export). Designations/skills, status, address, bank detail, and notes are **not** part of this folder - see the dedicated folders below for each. A worker's `kycStatus` and `faceEnrollment` are read-only summaries resolved from the separate `kyc`/`faceauth` modules, visible on Get/Create/Update's response but never editable here. **Delete Worker / Bulk Delete Workers live in the separate Worker Deletion folder at the end of this collection** - run everything else first.

request.description:
**Permission:** `workers.view`.

Paginated, filterable, sortable list of workers, returned as the lighter `WorkerSummaryResponse` (no signed photo URL, no full `faceEnrollment` object - see Get Worker for those).

**Filters** (all optional, all independent, repeat a query param for multiselect e.g. `?status=ACTIVE&status=REGISTERED`):
- `status`, `departmentId`, `industryId`, `designationId`, `skillId`, `kycStatus` - a non-empty filter matches ANY of its own values (OR within the filter); every non-empty filter is ANDed together with the others.
- `kycStatus` is resolved from the separate `kyc` module, not a column on this table - filtering by it costs one extra lookup query.
- `search` - free text against first/last name, mobile number, worker code, and email.

**Pagination/sort:** standard Spring pagination (`page`, `size`, `sort`). Default `page-size`/`max-page-size` are controlled centrally by `spring.data.web.pageable.default-page-size` / `.max-page-size` (100 / 500 at the time of writing, in `application.properties`) - not by this endpoint. Default sort is `createdAt,desc` (newest first) when `sort` is omitted. `sort` only accepts real, directly-queryable columns: `firstName`, `lastName`, `workerCode`, `mobileNumber`, `status`, `createdAt` - notably **not** `kycStatus` or any batch-resolved display name (e.g. `primaryDesignationName`), since those aren't columns on this table at all.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Unsupported `sort` property | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 |

request.description:
**Permission:** `workers.create`.

Creates a worker's core profile plus their initial designation(s)/skill(s). The new worker always starts at status `REGISTERED` (unless `aadhaarVerificationId` is given, in which case KYC verification auto-advances status to `ACTIVE` - see the second saved example below). Address and bank detail are **not** part of this request - use the dedicated sub-resource endpoints (Worker Address / Worker Bank Detail folders) once the worker exists.

**Validation, checked in this order:**
1. `mobileNumber` must be unique among active (non-deleted) workers.
2. `departmentId` must reference an existing department.
3. `industryId`, when given, must reference an existing industry.
4. `designationIds` - 1 to 3 ids, every one must exist, and `primaryDesignationId` must be one of them.
5. `skillIds` - each must belong to one of the selected `designationIds`.
6. `aadhaarVerificationId`, when given, must reference a verification that is `VERIFIED` and not already consumed; the whole creation fails otherwise (rolled back, no worker is left behind).

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| A referenced department/industry/designation id doesn't exist, or the designation/skill selection breaks a rule (e.g. more than 3 designations, `primaryDesignationId` not in `designationIds`, a skill outside the selected designations) | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 |
| `mobileNumber` already in use by another active worker | `CONFLICT` | 409 |

This request's Tests script saves the new id to `{{workerId}}` - every other folder in this collection needs it.

request.description:
**Permission:** `workers.edit`.

Replaces the worker's core profile fields (name, gender, DOB, mobile, email, department, industry). Designations/skills are untouched - use Worker Designations & Skills below. Same `mobileNumber` uniqueness and `departmentId`/`industryId` existence checks as Create, excluding this worker's own current row. Unlike Address/Bank Detail, this is **not** a progressively-optional request - `firstName`/`lastName`/`gender`/`mobileNumber`/`departmentId` are required on every call.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Unknown worker id | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |
| Another worker already has this `mobileNumber` | `CONFLICT` | 409 |
| Unknown `departmentId`/`industryId` | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 |

request.description:
**Permission:** `workers.export`.

**Returns a raw `text/csv` file download (`Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="workers.csv"`), NOT the usual JSON envelope** - this is the only endpoint on this controller that doesn't return `ApiResponse`. Columns, in order: Worker Code, First Name, Last Name, Mobile Number, Status, KYC Status, Designation (primary designation's display name, blank if none), Department, Face Enrolled (`Yes`/`No`).

Give `ids` for an exact set (unknown ids are silently skipped); otherwise every other field is an optional filter with the **exact same semantics as List Workers above** (a non-empty set matches ANY of its values; every non-empty field is ANDed together). Posting `{}` exports every worker, unfiltered. The whole CSV is built in memory, not streamed row-by-row - fine at today's admin-tool scale, called out here as a known, deliberate limitation.

item.name: Worker Status
item.description: The worker lifecycle: `REGISTERED -> KYC_PENDING -> ACTIVE <-> INACTIVE`, with `SUSPENDED` (temporary, no-fault hold) and `BLACKLISTED` (permanent ban) as two deliberately distinct paths off `ACTIVE` - legacy conflated all three into one inactive flag with no reason captured. Every change here takes an explicit target status via `workers.toggle_status` (single or bulk), never a blind toggle. `REGISTERED`/`KYC_PENDING` are reached only automatically (worker creation / KYC verification) and can never be set through this API; `ACTIVE` is reachable here only from `SUSPENDED`/`INACTIVE`, never from `REGISTERED`/`KYC_PENDING` (that requires completing KYC, which runs asynchronously outside any admin's request - see Worker KYC Bridge below). Entering or leaving `BLACKLISTED` additionally requires the caller to be a super-admin - un-blacklisting is exactly as high-privilege as blacklisting. Status History is the append-only, never-edited audit trail of every transition a worker has ever had, including the one this folder's own endpoints never make directly (the automatic KYC-verified → `ACTIVE` move, recorded with `changedBy: "system"`).

request.description:
**Permission:** `workers.toggle_status`.

An explicit target status, never a blind toggle - two quick calls can't race each other into an unpredictable end state this way.

**Rules:**
- `REGISTERED`/`KYC_PENDING` can never be set here - they're reached only automatically.
- Setting the status the worker is already in is rejected (no-op transitions are explicit errors, not silently accepted).
- A `reason` is **required** when the target is `SUSPENDED`, `BLACKLISTED`, or `INACTIVE`.
- `ACTIVE` is reachable here only from `SUSPENDED`/`INACTIVE` - from `REGISTERED`/`KYC_PENDING`, a worker becomes `ACTIVE` only by completing KYC verification (automatic, not via this endpoint).
- Entering **or** leaving `BLACKLISTED` requires the caller to be a super-admin - un-blacklisting is exactly as high-privilege as blacklisting.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Unknown worker id | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |
| Target is `REGISTERED`/`KYC_PENDING`, equals the current status, or `reason` missing for `SUSPENDED`/`BLACKLISTED`/`INACTIVE` | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 |
| Blacklist/un-blacklist attempted by a non-super-admin, or `ACTIVE` requested directly from `REGISTERED`/`KYC_PENDING` | `BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION` | 422 |

item.name: Worker KYC Bridge
item.description: A single endpoint bridging this controller to the separate `kyc` module: upgrades an **already-existing** worker's KYC using a successful Aadhaar e-KYC verification - the same mechanism Worker Profile's Create Worker uses when `aadhaarVerificationId` is given at creation time, exposed here separately for a worker who was onboarded manually and now wants to move to a live, API-verified KYC record. On success this publishes the same KYC-verified event that auto-advances status to `ACTIVE` when the worker is still `REGISTERED`/`KYC_PENDING` (see Worker Status above). Requires `workers.edit`. The verification itself is produced by the `kyc` module - see **ATW-Worker-KYC.postman_collection.json** for how `{{verificationId}}` is obtained; this request can be skipped if you don't have one yet, nothing else in this collection depends on it.

request.description:
**Permission:** `workers.edit`.

Upgrades an **already-existing** worker's KYC using a successful Aadhaar e-KYC verification - the same mechanism Create Worker uses when `aadhaarVerificationId` is given at creation time, exposed separately for a worker who was onboarded manually (e.g. via the kyc module's `submitAadhaar`) and now wants to move to a live, API-verified KYC record. On success, publishes the same KYC-verified event that auto-advances status to `ACTIVE` when the worker is still `REGISTERED`/`KYC_PENDING`.

**Errors:** the worker id must exist; the verification id must exist, be `VERIFIED` (not still pending or failed), and not already consumed by another worker.

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Unknown worker id, or unknown `verificationId` | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |
| Verification already consumed, or its Aadhaar number already belongs to another worker | `CONFLICT` | 409 |

item.name: Worker Photo
item.description: A worker's identity photo - not a KYC evidence document, so it gets the same small, image-only allowance as Masterdata's icons (contrast with the Document module's larger, PDF-inclusive limits used for KYC scans): `image/png`/`image/jpeg`/`image/webp` only, magic-byte cross-checked against the declared `Content-Type`, max 2MB, uploading when one already exists replaces it (old blob deleted). The returned `profilePhotoUrl` is a short-lived (~15 minute) signed URL - re-fetch rather than cache it. Both endpoints require `workers.edit`.

request.description:
**Permission:** `workers.edit`.

Multipart form-data with a single part, field name **`file`**. An identity photo, not a KYC evidence document, so it gets the same small, image-only allowance as Masterdata's icons (contrast with the Document module's larger, PDF-inclusive limits used for KYC scans):

1. File must be non-empty and **at most 2MB**.
2. Declared `Content-Type` must be exactly `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, or `image/webp`.
3. The file's actual leading bytes must match that declared type (magic-byte check) - a mismatch is rejected even if the `Content-Type` header looks fine.

Uploading a new photo when one already exists **replaces** it (the old blob is deleted). The returned `profilePhotoUrl` is a short-lived (~15 minute) signed URL - re-fetch rather than caching it.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Unknown worker id | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |
| Empty file, file over 2MB, disallowed/missing content type, or content doesn't match the declared type | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 |

item.description: Soft-delete only - sets `deletedAt`, never a real SQL `DELETE`; every satellite row (address, bank detail, designations, skills, notes, status history, KYC profile, face-biometric enrollment) is left completely untouched, preserving full history for audit/reconciliation. Both the single and bulk form require `workers.delete`. **Run these two requests last in this collection** - several folders above need `{{workerId}}` to still exist.

request.description:
**Permission:** `workers.delete`.

Soft-deletes a worker - sets `deletedAt`, never a real SQL DELETE. Every satellite row (address, bank detail, designations, skills, notes, status history, KYC profile, face-biometric enrollment) is left completely untouched, preserving full history for audit/reconciliation; nothing is cascaded away. The worker's mobile number becomes available again for a new worker to register with - a deliberate product decision. There is deliberately no restore/undelete endpoint yet.

**Refused unless the worker's current status is something other than ACTIVE** - change status first (e.g. to `INACTIVE`) via Change Worker Status, then delete. This is a deliberate, independent safety check, not a side effect of soft-delete.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Unknown worker id | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |
| Worker is still `ACTIVE` | `BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION` | 422 |

request.description:
**Permission:** `workers.delete`.

Applies the exact same guarded soft-delete as Delete Worker (above) to every id independently. Partial success is expected - an id that's still `ACTIVE`, or doesn't exist, is recorded in `failures[]` without rolling back the ids that already succeeded.

Request body is the shared `BulkIdsRequest` = `{ids: UUID[]}`, used identically by every bulk-delete endpoint across every module.

**Errors**

| Condition | Code | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| `ids` is empty | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 |

Note this endpoint always returns `200` - inspect `data.failures` for which ids weren't deleted.
